title: Finite coefficient realization identifies constructible witnesses and the specified derived exchange
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite discrete commutative ring and let $X'\xrightarrow{a}X$, $C\xrightarrow{c}Y$, $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to C$ be a chosen cartesian square of qcqs schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Put $A_T=p_T^*\underline A$. Use ordinary unbounded internal module derived categories with exact inverse images and ordinary derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention]. Let
$$E_T:D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_T})\simeq D(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},A)$$
be the termwise finite discrete coefficient equivalence [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence]. For every $L\in D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\underline A)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], there are $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},A)$ and an isomorphism $\nu_X^*M\cong E_XL$, where $\nu_X$ is site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; thus $E_XL$ carries an etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness].
The canonical comparisons identify the specified inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions under $E_T$, including their units, counits and pullback-composition maps. Consequently the following square commutes in the ordinary pro-etale derived category:
$$\begin{array}{ccc}E_C(c^*Rf_*L)&\xrightarrow{E_C(\operatorname{Ex}^{\rm int}_L)}&E_C(Rf'_*a^*L)\\ \downarrow\wr&&\downarrow\wr\\ c^{-1}Rf_*E_XL&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}^{\rm ord}_{E_XL}}&Rf'_*a^{-1}E_XL.\end{array}$$
Both horizontal maps are the unit--canonical square--counit mates [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], rather than arbitrarily chosen endpoint isomorphisms. The comparisons are natural in $L$. Properness and invertibility of either exchange are not assumed.

proof.text: Put $K=E_XL$. The finite-coefficient equivalence identifies bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories, so $K$ is bounded and each $\mathcal H^i(K)=E_X\mathcal H^i(L)$ ($E_X$ is termwise exact) has, on each stratum of a finite stratification of the qcqs scheme $X$ by constructible locally closed subschemes, a pro-etale cover on which it is $A_U\otimes_AP$ with $P$ a finitely presented $A$-module. Since $A$ is finite, $P$ is a finite $A$-module and $A_U\otimes_AP$ is the constant sheaf with value $P$, so the restriction to each stratum is locally constant with finite stalks; thus $K$ has bounded intrinsically constructible cohomology in the sense used by the origin theorem, with the same vanishing interval. Apply the arbitrary-finite-ring derived origin theorem to obtain $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},A)$ and $\alpha:\nu_X^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Retain this pair, which is the required etale-origin witness. Finite Tor amplitude is not needed for this existence assertion.

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived; coefficient translation through the cited equivalence

proof.text: Factor the underived realization as section-action reconstruction, change of ring by the finite constant-ring identification, and constant-scalar restriction. Internal operation transport identifies the first factor with the section-ring geometric adjunction. For the ring change, the coefficient-sections equality says that the ring isomorphisms commute with the adjunct coefficient maps for each edge $u$. Restriction of an action therefore sends $r\cdot m$ to the same action on $u_*M$ in either order; inverse image is its adjunction mate. Constant-scalar geometric adjunctions identify the last factor: their normalization hypothesis holds because the coefficient-sections equality takes every constant $a\in A$ to the same constant $a$. Composing gives natural comparisons $e_Vu^*_{\rm int}\cong u^{-1}e_T$ and $e_Tu_{*,\rm int}\cong u_*e_V$ identifying the ordinary Hom bijections, hence units and counits. Here $u:V\to T$ and $e$ denotes the heart equivalence whose termwise extension is $E$.

Apply compatible derived squares under exact equivalences to the ordinary comparisons of Step 2. This gives natural isomorphisms $b_u:E_T Ru_{*,\rm int}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*E_V$ commuting with the right-derived comparison units, and the termwise pullback comparisons $a_u:E_Vu^*_{\rm int}\xrightarrow{\sim}u^{-1}E_T$. To verify that these identify the independently specified derived adjunctions, apply the exact adjoint-square comparison theorem with $V=e_V$, $W=e_T$, $L=u^*_{\rm int}$, $L_0=u^{-1}$. Both left adjoints are exact by the conventions of the item and the heart comparison. The additional right-derived hypothesis is supplied by the preceding exact-equivalence derived square, including its universal pair and comparison unit. The theorem gives, for every $N$, $E_V(\varepsilon_{u,N})=\varepsilon^{\rm ord}_{u,E_VN}\circ u^{-1}(b_{u,N})\circ a_{u,Ru_*N}$ and the corresponding unit equation. Thus the comparisons preserve the actual derived units and counits on all unbounded objects.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; canonical exact-equivalence square and adjoint-square tools

proof.text: The ordinary direct-image compositor has the underlying sheaf composition map. Each direct-image comparison of Step 2 is identity on that same sheaf; hence the two composites around its comparison square are equal on every section. The internal pullback compositor is by definition the unique conjugate of this direct-image compositor under the specified adjunctions. On the ordinary side, the derived pullback compositor $c_{h,k}$ entering $\theta_\square$ is the class of the termwise canonical comparison of module pullbacks [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] (on K-flat complexes with flat terms, to which every object is isomorphic, so the natural isomorphism is determined there); that canonical comparison of composite left adjoints is the unique isomorphism carrying the single pullback unit to the two successive units [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], i.e. the conjugate of the ordinary identity-on-sections direct-image compositor. Since Step 2 identifies their Hom bijections, it identifies these conjugates as well. Pullback is exact, so apply the equality termwise to complexes and then localize: the exact-functor factorization uses these termwise representatives without resolutions. This proves compatibility of the derived pullback-composition maps. In particular, after the $a_u$ comparisons, the internal square map $\theta_\square:f'^*c^*\to a^*f^*$ becomes precisely the ordinary square map $f'^{-1}c^{-1}\to a^{-1}f^{-1}$ for the chosen equality $fa=cf'$.

proof.text:
Write $s_L:E_C(c^*Rf_*L)\xrightarrow{\sim}c^{-1}Rf_*E_XL$ for $a_c$ followed by $c^{-1}b_f$, and $t_L:E_C(Rf'_*a^*L)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*a^{-1}E_XL$ for $b_{f'}$ followed by $Rf'_*(a_a)$. By the exchange definition, the internal arrow is $\eta_{f'}$, followed by $Rf'_*(\theta_\square)$, followed by $Rf'_*a^*(\varepsilon_f)$. Substitute the unit and counit equations of Step 3 and the square equation of Step 4 in this three-factor composite. Naturality moves the $a_u,b_u$ past the intervening factors; consecutive inverse comparisons cancel. The resulting equality is
$$t_L\circ E_C(\operatorname{Ex}^{\rm int}_L)=\bigl(Rf'_*a^{-1}(\varepsilon^{\rm ord}_{f,E_XL})\circ Rf'_*(\theta^{\rm ord}_{\square,Rf_*E_XL})\circ\eta^{\rm ord}_{f',c^{-1}Rf_*E_XL}\bigr)\circ s_L=\operatorname{Ex}^{\rm ord}_{E_XL}\circ s_L.$$
This is the requested commutative square. All factors used are natural transformations, so the equality is natural in $L$. The calculation uses neither properness nor invertibility of a horizontal arrow.
